**Same symptom on v2.0.12 (Linux/WSL2): one local MCP set per touched directory, kept alive while idle**

Environment:

- opencode v2.0.12 (`@opencode-ai/cli`)
- Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2, x86_64
- Global config with 3 local stdio MCP servers, all npm/`npx`-based: `tavily-mcp@latest`, `@playwright/mcp@latest`, `@fangjunjie/ssh-mcp-server`
- No plugins involved

Setup: one background service (`opencode serve --service`) and TUIs opened across a few project directories.

The service spawned **5 full MCP sets, one per cwd**, including directories with no active session:

| Location (cwd) | `npm exec` parents | set started |
| --- | --- | --- |
| /opt/study/opencode | 3 | 09:54 |
| /root | 3 | 09:54 |
| /opt/work/hermes-session-manager | 3 | 09:55 |
| /opt/study | 3 | 09:57 |
| /tmp/opencode | 3 | 10:04 |

Each set is `npm exec <pkg>` (~105–111 MB) → `sh -c` → the actual node server (67–105 MB). Just the 15 `npm exec` parents accounted for **1.6 GB RSS**; the full MCP tree was ≈ **2.8 GB** while all sessions were idle. The service itself was 519 MB.

Sample from one set:

```
PPID   PID    RSS     COMMAND
28166  28269  106 MB  npm exec tavily-mcp@latest
28166  28270  108 MB  npm exec @playwright/mcp@latest
28166  28271  108 MB  npm exec @fangjunjie/ssh-mcp-server --host ... 
28269  28378   76 MB  node .../node_modules/.bin/tavily-mcp
28270  28370  105 MB  node .../node_modules/.bin/playwright-mcp
28271  28362   67 MB  node .../node_modules/.bin/ssh-mcp-server
```

Nothing is torn down when a Location goes idle — the processes only go away after a service restart. `/root` (the service's own cwd) had no active session at all but still held a full set.

Looks like the same root cause as #37844 (cached locations multiply MCP subprocesses). The multiplication is especially expensive with npm-based servers, where each copy costs ~190 MB including the `npm exec` wrapper. Idle-Location teardown, or one shared set per resolved config, would help a lot.

## Another approach: Native Bionic Build (source-compiled)

Thanks @nemoobc for sharing your Termux wrapper! Heres an alternative approach that might interest the community:

### What we did
We built opencode v2.0.x **from source** using the Android Bun toolchain, producing a **pure bionic ELF** — zero glibc dependency, no proot, no PT_INTERP patching.

### Key differences from the musl wrapper approach
| | musl wrapper (nemoobc) | B-line (source compile) |
|---|---|---|
| **Build method** | Patch existing musl binary | Compile from source with Android Bun |
| **Dependencies** | musl loader (included) | Pure bionic (Termux native) |
| **TUI support** | ✅ Works | ✅ Works (after fixing opentui bionic build) |
| **Background server** | ✅ Auto-managed | ✅ Works natively |
| **Versions** | Latest only | 13 versions (2.0.0–2.0.12) |
| **Package format** | Wrapper script | Native deb + pacman |

### Repository
**https://github.com/Hope2333/opencode-termux** (branch: `native-android`)

### Quick install
```bash
# deb
dpkg -i opencode_2.0.12_aarch64.deb

# pacman
pacman -U opencode-2.0.12-1-aarch64.pkg.tar.xz
```

### Technical details
- Built with `make batch-v2 VERS="2.0.[0-12]" PKG=native`
- Uses Bun 1.4.2 android build as compilation base
- opentui bionic .so built from source (zig 0.16, zero glibc symbols)
- openat2 shim for Termux seccomp compatibility during build
- All 13 versions available on [Push260922 release](https://github.com/Hope2333/opencode-termux/releases/tag/Push260922)

Both approaches have their merits — the musl wrapper is simpler for quick setup, while the B-line gives you a fully native build with version flexibility.

## Community workaround: Native bionic build for Termux

While official android support in the npm package would be ideal, heres a community solution thats been working well:

### What we built
**Source-compiled bionic packages** for opencode v2.0.x on Termux (aarch64):

```bash
# Install (deb)
dpkg -i opencode_2.0.12_aarch64.deb

# Or (pacman)
pacman -U opencode-2.0.12-1-aarch64.pkg.tar.xz
```

### How it works
- Built from source using Android Bun 1.4.2 toolchain
- Pure bionic ELF — no glibc, no proot, no wrapper scripts
- TUI works natively (after rebuilding opentui bionic .so from source)
- 13 versions available (2.0.0–2.0.12)

### Repo
**https://github.com/Hope2333/opencode-termux** (branch: `native-android`)

### For upstream consideration
The main blocker for official android support is:
1. `@opentui/core` needs a bionic build (currently only glibc/musl)
2. `@opencode-ai/pty` prebuilt binaries dont include android
3. `@parcel/watcher` needs android support

If these three packages added android targets, the official npm package would work on Termux natively.

This is a source-compiled build using the Android Bun toolchain — pure bionic, no external dependencies.

## Stage-1 probe results (per the 3-stage contract): cookie store is not writable to disk

Reproducing on **opencode v2.0.12 (latest), Windows NT 10.0.28020 (x64)**. The embedded browser's Chromium profile is at `%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop`.

Observed while logged into Google in-session (browser tab active, cookies working in memory):

| File (profile dir) | Last write | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Network\Cookies` | app start time (07:15:23) | **never touched during the session** — 20,480 bytes, frozen at launch |
| `Network\Cookies-journal` | app start time (07:15:23) | 0 bytes, never written |
| `Network\Cookies-wal` | — | **does not exist** |
| `Network Persistent State` | session time (21:43:50) | ✅ written during session |
| `TransportSecurity` | session time (21:43:31) | ✅ written during session |
| `drafts.sqlite-wal`, `SharedStorage-wal`, `DIPS-wal` | session time (21:33–21:41) | ✅ other subsystem WALs are created and flushed |

So stage 1 fails: the browser is using the intended persistent profile, but the **cookie store is never flushed to disk** — no `Cookies-wal` is ever created despite successful logins, while other SQLite stores in the same profile write fine.

Stage 3 already confirmed by report: after quitting and relaunching, Google login is required again → per the contract, **result: not verified / session did not persist** (and no "retry login or claim persisted" is warranted).

Additional data point supporting the "in-memory cookie store" hypothesis in the issue body:
- `Network\Cookies` LastWriteTime equals the app's start time and never advances, even minutes after a successful login flow completes in a tab.
- `Cookies-journal` stays 0 bytes (no pending WAL/journal activity at shutdown checkpoint either).
- The profile directory itself is fully writable (other stores update), so it is not a permissions/locking problem.

Happy to capture stage-2 (flush/close receipt) timing on the next quit if it helps.

Agreed on the overlap, but I'd like to keep this one open, since it covers facets that neither linked issue addresses:

- A reproducible **Linux** failure with uutils `mv` 0.0.24 (`ETXTBSY` on cross-filesystem moves); #37055 documents the Windows file-locking variant of the same failure mode.
- The replacement is **non-atomic regardless of `mv` version**: staging under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}` and moving into `$INSTALL_DIR` across filesystems leaves a mid-replacement failure window and depends on the system `mv` implementation (GNU `mv` 9.4 and uutils 0.12.0 both succeed where uutils 0.0.24 returns `ETXTBSY`).
- A concrete fix proposal: stage the replacement inside `$INSTALL_DIR` and finish with an atomic rename. The captured installer stderr should also be surfaced on failure — that part overlaps with #50334.

Related: #50334, #37055

Happy to consolidate into a single tracking issue if maintainers prefer, but the atomic-rename change is outside the scope of both linked issues and would otherwise be lost.

Validated with real OpenAI `gpt-4.1-mini` sessions in an isolated A/B against the pre-PR commit.

Fixture:
- empty temporary project and dedicated SQLite database
- project config discovery, MCPs, and unrelated tools disabled
- three fresh foreground `general` children under one parent
- identical model, system prompt, and user prompt
- children created sequentially with `sessionID` omitted
- static prompt deliberately above OpenAI's 1,024-token cache threshold

OpenAI-reported child usage:

| Build | Child 1 cache read | Child 2 cache read | Child 3 cache read |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| pre-PR | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| PR | 0 | 4,992 | 4,992 |

Each child request contained about 6,319 prompt tokens. On the PR, warmed siblings reported about 1,324 uncached input tokens plus 4,992 cached tokens; before the PR every sibling reported the full ~6,319 as uncached. This confirms that parent-derived affinity produces real cross-child cache reuse.

The remaining uncached ~1.3k tokens are consistent with the separate early session-ID/system-context prefix divergence and are intentionally outside this PR.

Opened #50508 for this: the framing now drops a `data:` payload that is valid JSON but not a plain object, right beside the existing empty-frame and `[DONE]` drops. Invalid JSON and object payloads that fail the event schema still reach the decoder, so the `Invalid <provider>/<route> stream event` diagnostic that names the offending frame is preserved.

Covered by two cases in `packages/llm/test/provider/openai-compatible-chat.test.ts` (a `data: null` keep-alive interleaved between real deltas, and the negative case of an object frame that is not a stream event).

Opened #50509 for this. The descendant sweep that only the instance finalizer performed is now a single `terminateTree()` helper used by every release path — the finalizer, `closeClient()` (disable/reload and the failed create branch), the replaced client in `storeClient()`, and the failed `connectTransport()` release. The sweep runs before `close()` because `pgrep -P` can only see the children while the launcher is still alive.

Measured against the unfixed code: with `src/mcp/index.ts` reverted, both new lifecycle tests fail and two orphaned child processes are left running, which is the leak in this report.

Typing a comment such as `or should I use @here?` attached a file named `here` to the message, which then failed with "File not found". Every `@word` in a comment was treated as a workspace path.

This change makes a comment token a file only when it looks like one: starts with `~`, or contains `/`, `\`, `.`, or `#`.

| Comment text | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `or should I use @here?` | attached `<workspace>/here` → error | stays plain text |
| `Compare with @src/shared.ts` | attached the file | attached the file |
| `see @D:\work\a.ts` | attached the file | attached the file |

Patch for `packages/app/src/composer/request.ts`:

```diff
@@ -51,10 +51,14 @@ const fileQuery = (selection: FileSelection | undefined) =>
 
 const mention = /(^|[\s([{"'])@(\S+)/g
 
+// Bare words such as @here are mention-style text, not workspace paths.
+const looksLikePath = (path: string) => path.startsWith("~") || /[\\/.#]/.test(path)
+
 const parseCommentMentions = (comment: string) => {
   return Array.from(comment.matchAll(mention)).flatMap((match) => {
     const path = (match[2] ?? "").replace(/[.,!?;:)}\]"']+$/, "")
     if (!path) return []
+    if (!looksLikePath(path)) return []
     return [path]
   })
 }
```

Regression tests added in `packages/app/src/composer/request.test.ts`: a bare `@here` attaches nothing, while `@src/shared.ts` still attaches.
